hypothesis.title: CT-based radiomics signature predicts high-risk neuroblastoma
hypothesis.intervention: Radiomics-derived imaging signature extracted from diagnostic CT scans
hypothesis.outcome: Accurate prediction of high-risk disease status
hypothesis.clinical_context: Risk stratification in newly diagnosed neuroblastoma to guide treatment intensity

steps.name: Define Study Objectives and Endpoints
steps.description: Formulate the primary objective: to assess the ability of a CT‑based radiomics signature to predict high‑risk neuroblastoma at diagnosis. Define primary endpoint (prediction accuracy measured by AUC) and secondary endpoints (sensitivity, specificity, positive/negative predictive values, calibration, and impact on treatment decision‑making).

steps.name: Form a Multidisciplinary Steering Committee
steps.description: Assemble pediatric oncologists, radiologists, medical physicists, data scientists, biostatisticians, ethicists, and patient advocates. The committee will oversee protocol development, data governance, and interim monitoring.

steps.name: Develop a Detailed Study Protocol
steps.description: Write a protocol that includes study design (prospective, multi‑center observational cohort), inclusion/exclusion criteria, sample size justification, imaging acquisition standards, radiomics workflow, statistical analysis plan, and data management procedures. Register the protocol on ClinicalTrials.gov before enrollment.

steps.name: Ethics and Regulatory Approvals
steps.description: Submit the protocol to the Institutional Review Boards (IRBs) of each participating center. Obtain informed‑consent forms appropriate for minors (parental consent and child assent). Secure data‑use agreements and comply with GDPR, HIPAA, and local regulations.

steps.name: Site Selection and Training
steps.description: Identify 8‑10 high‑volume pediatric oncology centers worldwide. Conduct standardized training webinars on CT acquisition parameters, DICOM handling, and radiomics pipeline to ensure uniformity across sites.

steps.name: Define Imaging Acquisition Parameters
steps.description: Standardize diagnostic CT scans: slice thickness ≥ 1.25 mm, 120 kVp, automatic exposure control, use of intravenous contrast per protocol, and breath‑hold or sedation as needed. Document scanner model, reconstruction algorithm, and kernel for later harmonization.

steps.name: Patient Enrollment
steps.description: Prospectively enroll consecutive children ≥ 18 years newly diagnosed with neuroblastoma, prior to any systemic therapy. Record baseline demographics, clinical stage, MYCN status, serum markers, and standard risk classification (INRG). Target N ≥ 500 patients to achieve >90 % power to detect an AUC difference of 0.05 compared with the standard model.

steps.name: Image Collection and Centralized Storage
steps.description: Upload raw DICOM CT scans to a secure, cloud‑based repository (e.g., REDCap‑Imaging or XNAT). Apply de‑identification pipelines and assign unique study IDs. Ensure backup and audit trails.

steps.name: Radiomics Feature Extraction Pipeline
steps.description: Develop a reproducible pipeline using IBSI‑validated software (e.g., PyRadiomics). Steps: (1) tumor segmentation – semi‑automatic 3‑D contour by two independent radiologists; (2) apply image resampling, intensity normalization, and discretization; (3) extract first‑order, shape, texture (GLCM, GLRLM, GLSZM, NGTDM), and wavelet features; (4) assess inter‑observer agreement (ICC>0.80) and retain robust features.

steps.name: Data Harmonization and Feature Reduction
steps.description: Apply ComBat or similar batch‑effect correction to mitigate scanner‑related variability. Perform dimensionality reduction: remove highly correlated features (r>0.9), then use supervised methods (LASSO, Elastic Net) within a nested cross‑validation framework to select the predictive signature.

steps.name: Model Development
steps.description: Combine the selected radiomics features with clinical variables (age, stage, MYCN) in logistic regression, random forest, and gradient boosting models. Use 5‑fold inner cross‑validation for hyper‑parameter tuning and outer 5‑fold cross‑validation for performance estimation.

steps.name: Internal Validation
steps.description: Assess discrimination (AUC, ROC curves) and calibration (calibration plots, Hosmer‑Lemeshow test) in the cross‑validated training cohort. Conduct decision‑curve analysis to evaluate clinical net benefit across risk thresholds.

steps.name: External Validation Cohort
steps.description: After the model is locked, test it on an independent cohort of ≥200 patients accrued at a subset of sites not involved in model training, following identical imaging and preprocessing steps. Report external AUC, sensitivity, specificity, and compare to the standard INRG risk classification.

steps.name: Statistical Analysis Plan Execution
steps.description: Use R or Python for all analyses. Compute confidence intervals for AUC via bootstrapping (2000 repetitions). Perform net reclassification improvement (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) versus the current risk model. Adjust for potential confounders (e.g., center) using mixed‑effects models.

steps.name: Safety Monitoring and Interim Analyses
steps.description: Although the study is observational, convene a Data Safety Monitoring Board (DSMB) to review enrollment rates, data completeness, and any unforeseen risks (e.g., excessive radiation exposure). No stopping rules are anticipated.

steps.name: Interpretation and Clinical Integration Workshop
steps.description: Organize a stakeholder workshop to discuss model results, usability in the clinic, and pathways for integrating the radiomics signature into multidisciplinary tumor boards. Develop a risk‑calculator web app for real‑time use.

steps.name: Manuscript Preparation and Dissemination
steps.description: Draft manuscripts for peer‑reviewed journals covering (1) development and internal validation, (2) external validation, and (3) health‑economic impact. Present findings at international pediatric oncology conferences (SIOP, ASCO‑Pediatric).

steps.name: Regulatory and Implementation Planning
steps.description: Engage with regulatory bodies (e.g., FDA, EMA) early to discuss qualification of the radiomics signature as a prognostic biomarker. Outline steps for prospective clinical utility trials where treatment intensity is guided by the signature.

steps.name: Long‑Term Follow‑up and Model Updating
steps.description: Continue to collect outcome data (event‑free survival, overall survival) for up to 5 years post‑diagnosis. Periodically recalibrate the model using new data (model updating) to maintain performance over time.
